name: Syndactyly Type 1

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Syndactyly Type 1

criteria.description: Presence of webbing or fusion between adjacent fingers or toes, primarily involving the 2nd and 3rd digits
Fusion limited to soft tissue without bony or nail involvement
No evidence of syndromic anomalies or systemic involvement

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of fusion of adjacent digits with cutaneous involvement without bony fusion, and exclusion of syndromic causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Radiographic imaging may be used to confirm absence of bony fusion

occasional.symptomName: Symphalangism affecting the phalanges of the hand

imaging: X-ray imaging showing absence of bony fusion between affected digits
genetic: Mutations in HOXD13 gene associated with some familial cases
Autosomal dominant inheritance pattern in familial cases
other: Physical examination revealing soft tissue webbing without nail or bone involvement

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of bony fusion or synostosis
Localized absence of skin rather than fusion
Presence of scalp or limb skin defects

redFlags: Presence of bony fusion indicating complex syndactyly
Associated syndromic features such as craniofacial anomalies
Functional impairment of hand or foot requiring urgent intervention
references: Temtamy SA, McKusick VA. The Genetics of Hand Malformations. 1978.
